# Summary: 2005 UK Government Manifesto

## Economic Policy

The manifesto emphasizes maintaining economic stability through low debt and high employment. Key commitments include:

- Maintaining the inflation target at two per cent
- Borrowing only to invest while keeping debt at prudent levels
- Continuing efficiency drives to liberate £21 billion for frontline services
- Pursuing an 80% employment rate as a long-term aim
- Raising the minimum wage to £5.35 by October 2006
- Reforming Incapacity Benefit with new work-focused requirements
- Supporting science investment to raise R&D spending from 1.9% to 2.5% of GDP by 2014
- Investing £180 billion in transport infrastructure through 2015

## Education

The education agenda focuses on personalized learning and specialist schools:

- Transforming all secondary schools into independent specialist schools
- Implementing a 15-year Building Schools for the Future program
- Expanding the Academies program to 200 schools by 2010
- Introducing Educational Maintenance Allowances for lower-income students
- Capping university fees at £3,000 annually (inflation-adjusted)
- Maintaining the 50% university participation target by 2010

## Crime and Security

On crime and community safety:

- Establishing neighborhood policing teams in every community
- Expanding Community Support Officers to 24,000
- Implementing compulsory drug testing at arrest for property and drugs offenders
- Introducing ID cards backed by biometric data
- Creating a points-based immigration system
- Establishing control orders for terrorism suspects

## Healthcare

NHS reforms include:

- Eliminating waits over 18 weeks from referral to treatment
- Providing patient choice of hospital
- Expanding primary care services and walk-in centers
- Developing NHS Foundation Trusts and independent sector capacity
- Restricting smoking in enclosed public places with exemptions for some pubs
- Improving school meals and introducing clearer food labeling

## Families and Pensions

Family support measures:

- Targeting halving child poverty by 2010-11
- Increasing paid maternity leave to nine months by 2007
- Expanding childcare with 3,500 Sure Start Children's Centres by 2010
- Increasing homeownership by one million
- Reforming pensions to address poverty while encouraging saving

## International Policy

Foreign policy priorities:

- Supporting EU membership and the Constitutional Treaty referendum
- Maintaining commitments in Iraq and Afghanistan
- Doubling international aid with a 2013 target for 0.7% of national income
- Leading on climate change with 60% carbon reduction target by 2050
- Supporting Middle East peace process

## Constitutional Reform

Democratic reforms include:

- Completing House of Lords reform
- Devolving more powers to Wales and London
- Giving neighborhoods new powers over local issues
- Establishing a Commission on Equality and Human Rights
- Working toward restored devolved government in Northern Ireland contingent on ending paramilitary activity
